html:
Ilham Tohti (born 1969) is a Uyghur economist who taught at Minzu University in Beijing and spoke for the rights of the Uyghurs of Xinjiang. In 2014 a Chinese court sentenced him to life in prison for separatism.

He studied the economy of Xinjiang and argued that Uyghurs were losing out: jobs went to Han migrants, and their religion and language were squeezed. He did not call for independence; he asked China to follow its own laws on regional autonomy. In 2006 he founded Uyghur Online, a website for debate on Uyghur issues.

After the July 2009 riots in Ürümqi he was held for weeks. He was arrested again in January 2014, tried in September and given a life sentence, and several of his students were jailed too. Little has been heard of him since. In 2019 the European Parliament gave him its Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought. His case came before the mass detention of Uyghurs in the internment camps from 2017.
